articles.title: 6-year-old Little League player Neven Coofer leaves lasting impact after sudden death in Kentucky
articles.summary: A Kentucky baseball community is mourning the sudden loss of 6-year-old Neven Coofer, a young Little League player remembered for his kindness, energy and
articles.body: A Kentucky baseball community is mourning the sudden loss of 6-year-old Neven Coofer, a young Little League player remembered for his kindness, energy and love for his older brother. Neven died unexpectedly in his sleep on Oct. 1, leaving his family, teammates and friends struggling to understand the loss. His family is still waiting for an official cause of death. In the days since, people across Lexington have come together to remember a boy whose presence brought joy to those around him. A community fundraiser is also helping his family manage the difficult days ahead.Neven Coofer remembered as a beloved Little League playerNeven began playing baseball at age four in the Southeastern Cal Ripken Baseball League. Though he was still very young, league officials said he quickly became one of the most familiar faces at the ballpark.Aaron Anderkin, vice president of the league, described the impression Neven made on everyone around him.“If you had to think of one six-year-old at this park that everyone knew, that they gravitated towards, that just had an infectious personality, it was Neven.”His family remembers that warmth in equally personal terms. Neven’s mother, Gordana Coofer, said her son was full of happiness and described him in words that captured the depth of her loss.“Neven was everything that was good in this world,” his mom, Gordana Coofer told Fox 56, adding that she remembered her son as “happy.”His father, Dominick Coofer, also spoke about the close bond Neven shared with his 8-year-old brother, Niko. Neven often watched his brother play baseball, taking photos and videos on his iPad.“He’s his brother’s biggest cheerleader,” his father, Dominick Coofer, told the outlet about Neven’s older brother, Niko, 8. “There’s pictures of him with his iPad getting pictures of his brother and videos of his brother playing baseball.”Kentucky community rallies around Neven Coofer’s familyThe family said Neven had a history of febrile seizures and had been diagnosed with Kawasaki disease, an inflammatory condition that can affect blood vessels and, in some cases, the heart. However, no official cause of death has been announced.His death has also brought an outpouring of memories from people who knew him. Niko returned to the baseball field on Oct. 5, stepping up to the plate in his brother’s memory.“If you were sad, he would come up to you and ask if you were okay,” Niko said.A GoFundMe campaign has since been created to support the Coofer family as they navigate the financial and emotional weight of their loss. The fundraiser describes Neven as a child who brought “so much light, love, and joy” to those around him.For a community that watched him grow through baseball, his absence is difficult to put into words. articles.title: “Every kid deserves that same opportunity”: How Paige Bueckers’ $50,000 gesture for wildfire-hit youth sports shows her giving goes beyond basketball
articles.summary: Paige Bueckers has found another way to use basketball to help young athletes.
articles.body: Paige Bueckers has found another way to use basketball to help young athletes. On March 14, 2025, the UConn star committed $50,000 to Good Sports’ Restore Play LA Recovery Fund, supporting youth sports programs affected by the devastating Los Angeles wildfires. The money went toward equipment, apparel and footwear so children in hard-hit communities could get back to their sports programs.The contribution came with a simple idea behind it. Bueckers knows what sports can give a young person, and she wanted children dealing with the aftermath of the fires to have that same chance. Her work with Good Sports also showed this was not her first effort to put resources into youth sports.Paige Bueckers put $50,000 behind Los Angeles youth sports recoveryThe January 2025 wildfires caused widespread damage across Los Angeles, and youth sports programs also lost equipment and resources. Good Sports created Restore Play LA to help those programs replace what they needed to resume activities.Bueckers committed $50,000 to the effort in partnership with Good Sports and Gatorade. The organization planned to provide items such as basketballs, cleats, jerseys, nets and other essential gear to programs serving young people in the affected areas.Bueckers explained the personal side of the donation in Good Sports’ March 14 announcement.“Basketball has given me so much more than just a game,” Bueckers said in the announcement. “It’s given me a community, confidence, and a space to dream big.”She then pointed to the children who had lost access to those opportunities because of the fires.“Every kid deserves that same opportunity, no matter their circumstances,” Bueckers said in the same announcement.The goal went beyond replacing a few balls or uniforms. Good Sports said the initiative would focus on underserved communities in the areas hit hardest by the fires. The organization also viewed sports as a way for children to regain routine, connection and confidence during recovery.Paige Bueckers support for young athletes started before the LA wildfiresThe $50,000 donation added to a longer relationship between Bueckers and Good Sports. During her time at UConn, she had already helped the nonprofit provide more than $65,000 worth of new sports equipment and apparel to underserved youth programs in Washington, D.C., Minneapolis and Montana.That work included a surprise unveiling for a girls’ basketball team in Hartford, Connecticut.So the Los Angeles donation was not an isolated move. Bueckers had already used opportunities created by her basketball career to help young athletes who needed better access to sports.The impact of Restore Play LA continued well beyond Bueckers’ original contribution. By January 2026, Good Sports said the broader Restore Play effort had shipped 65 donations worth more than $1.54 million and served 34,471 children. The organization said the support helped schools reopen programs and community groups resume activities after the fires.For Bueckers, the message stayed simple. Basketball gave her confidence, community and a place to dream. Her $50,000 contribution helped give young athletes affected by the Los Angeles fires a chance to keep finding those same things through sports.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Connor McDavid and Lauren Kyle’s $100,000 donation changes the lives of thousands of cancer stricken children in Edmonton
articles.summary: Connor McDavid, the Edmonton Oilers captain, and his wife, Lauren Kyle, have remained dedicated to Edmonton as they have often spoken about their love and
articles.body: Connor McDavid, the Edmonton Oilers captain, and his wife, Lauren Kyle, have remained dedicated to Edmonton as they have often spoken about their love and passion for the city. While Connor McDavid has his focus on the new season on the ice even though the team has experienced a slow start, his donation changed the life of a young fan’s family and helped in more research in cancer.Connor McDavid gave away $100,000 after a six year old fan’s death as Lauren Kyle stood by himIn 2022, Connor McDavid pledged to donate $100,000 towards the fund of Ben Stelter, who passed away tragically after a tough battle against cancer.Ben Stelter, a six year old boy, was a dedicated fan of the Edmonton Oilers and the captain Connor McDavid’s donation to his fund changed lives of many children.On a social media post, the Edmonton Oilers’ star captain Connor McDavid wrote, “I am teaming with @ashifmawji and family to pledge $100,000 towards the newly launched Ben Stelter Fund, to get better outcomes for youth that are battling cancer. We challenge all athletes, individuals and businesses to be a part of this!”In an interview, Connor McDavid said, "He was an amazing little guy who lit up every single room he was in…”The star captain added, “He certainly lit up our room any time he walked in there."As Connor McDavid partnered with the Edmonton social entrepreneur and investor, Ashif Mawji and his family for the pledge, Mawji said, "The Ben Stelter Fund will focus on four key pillars. The first one is magical experiences for kids battling cancer. The next one is at home medical equipment for these families. “Edmonton social entrepreneur and investor, Ashif Mawji added, “The third one is outcome-based research to help find a cure for Glioblastoma and other types of cancers that kids face. The final one is venture-based philanthropy, which is where we invest in projects, ventures and other initiatives that infuse entrepreneurship to help find a cure for cancer…”Connor McDavid’s wife, Lauren Kyle, has been a strong support by his side as he focuses on the new seasonIn many of their interviews, both Connor McDavid and his wife, Lauren Kyle, have often spoken about how they plan on living in Edmonton for the rest of their lives and build a family here.Through all his philanthropic activities, Connor McDavid’s wife, Lauren Kyle, has been a strong support by his side.Connor McDavid’s wife, the popular entrepreneur and interior designer, Lauren Kyle, has also often spoken about how difficult it is to be there for an athlete through all the challenging days and how she has to “show up” for him.For now, Connor McDavid remains committed to the new season.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Dream move within one win of first WNBA Finals appearance since 2013 after overtime victory
articles.summary: Angel Reese scored six overtime points and Naz Hillmon's go-ahead layup gave the Atlanta Dream a 2-0 WNBA semifinals lead over the New York Liberty.
articles.body: Atlanta’s perfect postseason run continued Wednesday night before a raucous home crowd. The Dream moved within one win of their first WNBA Finals appearance since 2013 when Naz Hillmon’s go-ahead layup with just 20.8 seconds remaining in overtime lifted Atlanta to a 101-98 victory over the New York Liberty and a 2-0 lead in the semifinal series. Angel Reese, the 2026 WNBA Defensive Player of the Year, scored 23 points, including six of Atlanta’s 13 points in overtime. She then made two free throws with less than five seconds remaining after Sabrina Ionescu’s errant pass, helping the Dream hold off the defending champions. Jordin Canada also scored 23 points and added eight assists for Atlanta, which won Game 1, 92-82. NEW YORK LIBERTY VS ATLANTA DREAM PREVIEW: WHY THE INTERIOR MATCHUP COULD DECIDE THIS WNBA SHOWDOWN Breanna Stewart led the Liberty with 35 points, but she missed a desperation attempt on the game’s final play. With the Liberty trailing 86-80 and less than two minutes remaining in regulation, Sabrina Ionescu buried a deep 3-pointer to cut Atlanta’s lead to three. An Atlanta shot-clock violation with 31 seconds left gave New York another opportunity, and Breanna Stewart finished a layup through traffic to make it 86-85. WNBA LEGEND BREANNA STEWART OPENS UP ON REPRESENTING AMERICA AT FIBA WOMEN'S WORLD CUP The Dream were already without Allisha Gray, their leading scorer, who was ruled out of Game 2 with a hand injury. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Gray, a four-time All-Star, injured her left hand during the first quarter of Atlanta’s 92-82 Game 1 victory over the New York Liberty. She briefly returned to action after going to the locker room, but went down a second time after diving for a loose ball and did not return. Wednesday marked the first game Gray had missed this season, but Atlanta received key contributions off the bench to shoulder the scoring burden. Game 3 is scheduled for 7:30 p.m. Friday at Barclays Center in Brooklyn, New York. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: Candace Parker finally reveals Caitlin Clark’s heated playoff moment after the Fever star screamed at the WNBA legend
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark hit a big three against the Aces, turned toward the scorer's table, and screamed at Candace Parker.
articles.body: Caitlin Clark hit a big three against the Aces, turned toward the scorer's table, and screamed at Candace Parker. The WNBA legend was sitting there minding her own business. Parker has now explained what she heard, and the answer includes a pointed question and one swear word that cannot be printed here. She went through it on Wednesday's Post Moves podcast, which she co-hosts with Clark's Fever teammate Aaliyah Boston, and kept things light with a Steph Curry comparison. Las Vegas won the first-round series 2-1 and eliminated the Fever.What did Caitlin Clark yell at Candace Parker?Candace Parker was telling the story to Aaliyah Boston. She was at the scorer's table, she said, when Clark knocked down the three and turned on her. Parker was unsure of the exact words, so she tried two versions out loud. Did Clark ask what she thought this was, or did a curse word sit in the middle of the question?Parker went with the second. Boston, laughing, confirmed it. Parker's own reaction was simple. She wanted to say great shot, keep things moving, and go back to sitting there.The pair had already settled it in person. After the game, cameras appeared to catch the Fever point guard telling Parker, "I blacked out," and both laughed it off.Parker gave the moment some context. She pointed to a night years ago when Curry hit a shot and walked over to Reggie Miller, who was calling the game, to say something. Same energy, she said, and she found it cool. The three-time Finals champion added that she wanted opponents to do exactly this when she played. She asked for the trash talk and the finger in her face because it fired her up. Some players feed off chaos, in Parker's view, and she used to be one of them. Her verdict on Clark's outburst was short.How much did WNBA playoff viewership drop after the Fever lost?The Fever's exit set off a ratings argument almost right away. A post on X claimed the playoffs lost 70 to 76 percent of their viewers once Clark was gone. It had no source and passed a million views in about 18 hours. Other accounts pushed the figure as high as 78 percent.The fairer comparison is Game 1 of Fever-Aces against the two Game 1s of the semifinals, played Sunday. USA Today reporter Christine Brennan posted the numbers: 2.11 million viewers for Fever-Aces on ABC, 1.17 million for Liberty-Dream on ABC, and 1.12 million for Aces-Valkyries on NBC and Peacock. Front Office Sports reporter Colin Salao shared the same figures. By that math, the drop is 44 to 47 percent.It is still a big fall, but it is well short of the viral claims. Each semifinal opener still pulled more than a million viewers, and four teams are chasing the title.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Sportspersons, including Ajinkya Rahane, Shikhar Dhawan and many others, paid tribute to veteran actor Nana Patekar following his death on Thursday.Former India captain Rahane remembered Patekar’s contribution to cinema and praised the impact of his work over the years. In a post on X, Rahane described the veteran actor as a “truly remarkable actor”.“Nana Patekar ji was a truly remarkable actor whose work has inspired and entertained generations. Very sad to hear about his passing. May his soul rest in peace,” he said.Dhawan also expressed his grief over Patekar’s death. The former India opener called him a special talent and said his work would continue to inspire generations.“Indian cinema has lost a truly special talent today. Nana Patekar saab, your work will continue to inspire generations. Om Shanti.” Dhawan said in an X post.Patekar’s contribution to cinemaPatekar was a prominent figure in Hindi and Marathi cinema. He began his acting career with the 1978 film ‘Gaman’ and went on to earn widespread recognition through several acclaimed performances.Some of his notable films include ‘Parinda,’ ‘Prahar,’ ‘Angaar,’ ‘Krantiveer,’ ‘Tiranga,’ ‘Khamoshi’ and ‘Ab Tak Chhappan,’ among others.Patekar continued to remain active in the film industry in recent years. articles.title: Fan interference in Yankees-Rays game brings back bad Astros' memory for Alex Bregman
articles.summary: During the Yankees' playoff loss, Alex Bregman tweeted about a fan interference call that had him furious when he was with the Astros. He quickly deleted the...
articles.body:
Alex Bregman probably was just trying to begin the early days of his offseason by relaxing with some playoff baseball on the TV when what he saw Wednesday night gave him flashbacks to a rough night in Denver more than eight years ago.

The New York Yankees were swept by the Tampa Bay Rays in the American League Division with a 4-3 loss that was marred by a fan interference call that went against the home team. In Game 3 of the ALDS, Yankees infielder Anthony Volpe thought he had hit a game-tying two-run homer in the sixth inning, but the call was overturned by replay when a fan was ruled to have reached over the left-field wall and snagged the ball over the glove of Rays' left fielder Victor Mesa Jr. After a lengthy review, umpires ruled the ball would not have cleared the fence but also wouldn't have been caught, so Volpe was given a double, and the runner from first was allowed to score. Volpe, however, was left stranded at the end of the inning.

All of that had Bregman, who finished his first season with the Chicago Cubs last week by getting swept by the San Diego Padres in the wild-card round, thinking back to his Astros days.

"I hit that same ball LF in 2018 at Coors … They called me out after review from fan interference," Bregman posted on Twitter immediately after the play before eventually deleting the tweet. "Has there been a fan interference rule modification since? I want my double."

Bregman, who rarely posts on Twitter these days, concluded the post with two crying laughing emojis, but the former Astros star wasn't laughing in 2018.

"It was a f- joke," he told the Houston Chronicle on July 25, 2018 . "And they should be f- ashamed of themselves."

On that night, Bregman led off the sixth inning with a ball deep to left. Rockies left fielder Gerardo Parra leaped backwards and reached his glove above the wall, only for a fan wearing an Astros' Justin Verlander jersey to reach out and have the ball nick his glove and land on the warning track while Bregman raced to third for what he thought was a leadoff triple.

After Rockies manager Bud Black asked for the play to be reviewed, replay officials in New York determined the Astros fan had prevented Parra from making the catch and ruled Bregman out. Bregman was irate, flinging his helmet and yelling at the umpires as Astros manager A.J. Hinch came out to argue.

The difference from the call in Wednesday's Yankees-Rays call is that replay officials in 2018 ruled that Parra could have made the catch against the Astros, which only further infuriated Bregman following the game, which Houston lost 3-2 on a ninth-inning walkoff.

"Obviously the guy has never played f- baseball before in his life, the guy in charge of whoever made that decision," Bregman said that night. "There is no possible way you can say a left fielder jumping backwards into a wall is guaranteed to make a catch. It changed the whole f- game. We're up 2-1 at the time, I'm at third base. We need a fly ball to the outfield to get me in and it's 3-1. It's f- horrible."

The Astros, who were defending World Series champions at the time, still went on to reach the American League Championship Series that year and the 24-year-old Bregman had an excellent season, hitting .286 with 31 home runs and 103 RBIs. He also led all of baseball with 51 doubles.

articles.title: Silcock relishing European Championships chance
articles.summary: Jersey table tennis player Hannah Silcock says she is relishing the chance to take on Europe's best later this month.
articles.body:
Jersey table tennis player Hannah Silcock says she is relishing the chance to take on Europe's best later this month.

The 19-year-old will represent the island at the European Championships in Slovenia - the first time she has competed at the senior event.

Silcock is ranked 340th in the world in women's singles and 135th in Europe.

It comes after she played in the European Junior Championships in July, where she reached the last 64 in the mixed doubles after an early exit in the singles.

"It's my first senior Europeans. I played the junior Europeans in the summer, now a first senior competition I think it's just seeing how I get along against these players," she told BBC Radio Jersey

"I'm just trying to pick up a few good wins here and there and just kind of get a feel for it really."

Silcock rose to national attention at the 2022 Commonwealth Games when she pushed top-ranked England player Tin Tin Ho in the last 32 of the women's singles before losing 4-2 at the age of 15.

She has recently been training alongside Great Britain's elite players in Sheffield in the build-up to the European Championships, as well as playing in France and Sweden.

Silcock has risen up the world rankings in the past year - she is the sixth-best ranked British woman in the world.

It is an improvement she puts down to opting to concentrate fully on the sport, and is ranked 110th in the junior world rankings.

"Taking a year out just to focus on playing table tennis has definitely enhanced my game," she explained.

"I went to Japan for a couple of weeks in the summer which was amazing and the training was so good - I feel like it's definitely improved my game.

"I've seen a big jump in the rankings, so I've put myself in a good position and I'm really looking forward to seeing what comes next."

articles.title: Jeffrey Maier’s Yankees Lore Returns on Anthony Volpe HR That Doesn’t Count
articles.summary: It was New York Yankees legend Yogi Berra who once coined the phrase, “Deja vu all over again.” Yes, that’s redundant, but that’s what made it such a famous...
articles.body:
It was New York Yankees legend Yogi Berra who once coined the phrase, "Deja vu all over again."

Yes, that's redundant, but that's what made it such a famous Yogi-ism — and it may never have applied better than on Wednesday night in the Bronx.

Anthony Volpe hit a fly ball deep to left field — really the only difference about this play, making it more of a mirror scene to 30 years earlier. A fan reached over the fence and deflected it. The umpires had to make a controversial ruling.

At least for baseball fans of a certain age, it brought to mind Jeffrey Maier.

Jeffrey Maier was a 12-year-old fan in the right field bleachers during Game 1 of the 1996 ALCS as the Yankees hosted the Baltimore Orioles .

With the Yankees down a run, Derek Jeter hit a fly ball to right field in the eighth inning.

Replays later showed the ball wasn't going to leave the ballpark, but Maier, seated in the front row, reached out his glove and deflected it away from the Orioles right fielder, Tony Tarasco.

The umpires gathered and ruled it a home run.

By the book, it should've been fan interference, but the umpires didn't make that call.

Jeter was credited with a game-tying solo home run, and eventually that season, the Yankees went on to win the World Series.

Maier was famous in the Bronx, and an enemy for fans of the Orioles.

His impact is part of what made the call on Wednesday night for Volpe different.

Volpe's fly ball was also touched by a fan in front of the wall as it dropped to earth.

This time, though, the umpires had instant replay — and the legacy of the incorrect Jeffrey Maier call hanging over their head.

They didn't get this one wrong. They called it fan interference, but based on everyone's positioning on the play, they gave Volpe a double.

The Yankees had been down two, and it would've been a two-run homer to tie it, 4-4.

Instead, the Yankees remained down 4-3 with Volpe awarded second base.

Volpe was then stranded at second when Spencer Jones struck out swinging.

For a moment, the Yankees appeared to have tied the game, and then it swung the other way.

It was almost a bit of universal karma for what had happened with Maier 30 years ago.

There are many Yankees fans who weren't even alive when Maier once managed to get Jeter a home run that was never going to leave the ballpark.

They were alive for this one, though, and it went in reverse — the Yankees had a run taken off the board.

And given that a loss on Wednesday night could end the Yankees' season, this moment could cost them the chance to play deeper into October.

articles.title: NLCS Bound: Strong pitching, home run robbery by Mitchell leads Brewers to Game 4 win
articles.summary: The pitching staff held the Padres to one run and three hits, and Garrett Mitchell had the home run robbery of the year
articles.body:
The Brewers are heading back to the NLCS. An all-around strong game by the Brewers led them to a 3-1 win over the Padres, ending the series in four games and setting up a rematch from last season.

The game started out looking rough for the Brewers. In the top of the first, Jackson Chourio, Christian Yelich, and William Contreras went down on six pitches. Meanwhile, the Padres put the pressure on right away. After Fernando Tatis popped out on the first pitch Robert Gasser threw, Jackson Merrill hit a one out single to right-center. Manny Machado then surprised everyone with a bunt, and it was perfectly placed for a single.

Next up was Ty France, and he hit what looked like a double-play ball to Joey Ortiz. He took the out at first himself, but did not throw to first. It's not clear why he didn't go for it, but it was the second out of the inning. Gasser then walked Austin Hays on five pitches, loading the bases for Xander Bogaerts. However, Gasser recovered and got Bogaerts to pop out, ending the inning.

Both teams traded scoreless second innings. Jake Bauers drew a one-out walk, but Cooper Pratt grounded into a double play to end the inning. Meanwhile, Gasser recovered with an efficient inning, retiring the side on 12 pitches while striking out one.

In the third, Brewers' baseball was on full display. Sal Frelick led off the inning with a single that Jake Cronenworth managed to knock down and keep in the infield. Frelick then stole second, and Garrett Mitchell brought him in with an RBI single to center. For the first time in the series, the Brewers scored first, leading 1-0.

They had a chance to add on more, but Ortiz grounded into a double play for the first two outs of the inning. Chourio drew a two-out walk after that, but Yelich grounded out to end the top of the inning.

The lead wouldn't hold up long, unfortunately. Tatis Jr. led off the bottom of the third, and hit the fourth pitch he saw 429 feet out to center field, tying the game at 1-1. Gasser recovered by retiring the next three batters he saw, keeping the game tied.

The Brewers kept the pressure on in the fourth. Contreras singled to start the inning, which ended Walker Buehler's day. He pitched 3+ innings and allowed just the one run, allowing three hits and two walks with no strikeouts. Robbie Ray was first in out of the bullpen for the Padres. He allowed a one-out walk to Bauers, but that was it as he got out of the inning.

Gasser got one more inning for the Brewers, and despite an error by Pratt that allowed Campusano to reach, he got out of the inning without issue. Gasser gave the Brewers four strong innings, allowing just one run, three hits, and a walk while striking out three.

Mitchell started out the fifth inning with a big hit for the Brewers, tripling to right to give the Brewers a leadoff runner for the third straight inning. This time, the Brewers would not strand him. After Ortiz grounded out, Chourio hit a single to center and brought in Mitchell. The Brewers had the lead back, 2-1. Yelich added a single in the fifth, that was it.

Aaron Ashby was the first reliever out of the bullpen for the Brewers in the bottom of the fifth. He didn't run into any issues, retiring the side in order on nine pitches. He also got some help from Pratt, who recovered from his earlier error with a nice play to get Tatis Jr.

Meanwhile, the Brewers offense kept going. Bauers led off the sixth with a single, the fourth straight inning where the Brewers had their leadoff man on. Pratt then kept up his redemption his a hard-hit ball down the left field line, which bounced out over the wall for a ground-rule double. Frelick was up next, and hit one deep to left, but remained in the park. It was more than deep enough to score Bauers, and the Brewers added a critical insurance run, making it a 3-1 game.

Ashby remained in the game for the sixth, and despite allowing a walk to Ty France, a double play made it a 1-2-3 inning, with Ashby just needing 12 pitches in that inning. The Padres chose to go to Mason Miller in the seventh inning as the top of the Brewers' lineup was due up. He started out strong with a line out of Chourio and strikeout of Yelich — the first strikeout by a Padres' pitcher in the game. Miller faltered after that, allowing back-to-back singles to Contreras and Turang. Bauers then drew his third walk of the game, reaching base for the fourth time and loading them. Pratt had a chance to do some damage, but he lined out to center to end the inning. He also burned the Brewers' last ABS challenge in the at-bat.

In a surprise move, Ashby remained in the game for the seventh inning. He had thrown just 21 pitches through two innings and was still in good shape. He got Bogaerts to ground out and Campusano to strike out for the first two outs of the inning. He then walked pinch-hitter Miguel Andujar, bringing up Samad Taylor. Ashbe froze Taylor with a four-pitch strikeout, finishing up three excellent innings for the Brewers' bullpen.

After the Brewers went down in order against Joe Musgrove in the eighth, it was Abner Uribe for the ninth with the top of the lineup due up. The inning did not start out well with Tatis Jr. drawing a walk in an at-bat that Contreras wanted to challenge a couple pitches, but could not because the Brewers were out. Uribe recovered with a strikeout of Merrill, bringing up Machado. On the second pitch, Machado hit a ball to deep center field that was going to leave the park for a game-tying home run. However, Mitchell denied him, making a leaping grab to rob Machado and keep the Brewers ahead.

France popped out after that and morale for the Padres was at a low for the series. The Brewers were three outs away from the NLCS.

They couldn't tack on in the top of the ninth, though they did have another scoring chance. Yelich was hit by a pitch hit one out, and stole second base. Turang sent one to deep left field, but it wasn't deep enough and the inning ended.

Trevor Megill came in for the ninth inning to close the game out. Jacob Misiorowski was also throwing in the bullpen just in case. Megill began with a four-pitch strikeout of pinch-hitter Ethan Salas. Bogaerts was up next and worked the count full, but ended with a groundout to Ortiz for the second out. Gavin Sheets was called in as a pinch-hitter with two outs and the Brewers needing one more out. Megill started with two balls, came back with two strikes, then got Sheets to strike out looking and end the game, sending the Brewers to the National League Championship Series.

The pitching staff was the star of the game. Their four pitchers held the Padres to one run, three hits, and four walks. They also struck out nine. After Tatis Jr.'s home run, the Brewers did not allow another hit in the game. Gasser pitched four innings and allowed one run, Ashby had three scoreless, and Uribe and Megill each had a scoreless inning each. The big assist goes to Mitchell, who robbed Machado of a home run and two runs on the board.

Meanwhile, the Brewers' offense was balanced, recording ten hits and four walks. Contreras and Mitchell had two-hit days. Bauers reached base in all four of his plate appearances. The only Brewer that did not reach base was Ortiz.

The Brewers now get a few days off before the NLCS starts on Sunday. The opponent will be the Dodgers, once again. The Dodgers won the series against the Braves in four games earlier today. This will be the third time in the last nine years the teams face off in the NLCS. First pitch on Sunday is at 7 p.m. on FOX, and you have to expect that the starter will be Jacob Misiorowski.

articles.title: England goalkeeper Jordan Pickford ‘would love nothing more’ than to see Bayern Munich’s Harry Kane lift Ballon d’Or
articles.summary: Pickford supports his international teammate.
articles.body:
As the season changes into fall, we move on into October. October means many things for many different people, but, to a large section of football fans, it is defined as the month the Ballon d'Or is awarded. This year, England captain and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane is rumored to be one of the frontrunners to win the award, which no English player has won in around 25 years. Kane did score 73 goals for club and country combined last season, after all, earning the shout with his ridiculous form.

Asked about his skipper's chances to win the award, England goalkeeper Jordan Pickford supported Kane's claim to the award.

"I think he is right in the mix for it, the standards he has for himself and the goals he has scored are second to none, his all-round character as a lad is a great example to anyone in football to set the standards he does, that's why he gets the rewards," Pickford mused at the press conference ahead of England's clash with Croatia (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ). "I'd love nothing more than to see him lift the Ballon d'Or. I think it would be a credit to him and his family and all the work they have done. It will be great for Harry if he gets it. It could be a great couple of months for the skipper and it's fully deserved. Hard work pays off, that's the message."

articles.title: Dies Janse Believes Ajax Teammate Can Help Him Improve: "A Real Beast"
articles.summary: Dies Janse believes that one of his Ajax teammates can help him improve.
articles.body:
Will Ajax win the Eredivisie this season?

Ajax overhauled their central defence during the summer transfer window.

Josip Sutalo moved to Lazio on an initial loan deal, and the Italian side has the option to make the transfer permanent next summer. Ko Itakura also returned to Borussia Mönchengladbach after a disappointing year in Amsterdam, and Ahmetcan Kaplan moved to NEC Nijmegen on a permanent transfer after a successful loan spell there last season.

To replace those players, Ajax brought Daley Blind back to the club on a free transfer for his third spell at Ajax, following the expiry of his contract at Girona. Ajax also signed Thilo Kehrer on loan from AS Monaco, and Dies Janse returned to the club following a successful loan spell last season at FC Groningen.

Janse started 30 games in the Eredivisie last season for Groningen, and his performances attracted interest from European clubs, including reportedly Club Brugge.

Ajax were adamant, however, that Janse was not for sale, and he recently signed a contract extension with the club, keeping him at the Johan Cruijff ArenA until June 2030.

Tolu Arokodare has made a huge impact in the early stages of the season. The Nigerian striker has scored six goals in nine appearances in all competitions and has been one of Ajax's standout performers.

In an interview with Sportnieuws.nl , Janse revealed that he believes facing Tolu in training can help him become a better centre-back.

"The training level at Ajax is incredibly high," Janse explained.

"Some guys have joined me from whom I can learn a whole lot. So I'm in a good place to develop myself further."

Janse was asked what aspects of his game he believes he can improve.

"Actually, there is something to gain in every area," Janse said.

"Physically, turning and twisting, and getting stronger. Well, if I can face Tolu, that can only be a good thing. He is a real beast."

Jordi Cruijff has received some criticism for building an Ajax team that is particularly focused on winning in the short term, as opposed to the long term. Janse's contract extension, however, is an example that Cruijff is also trying to ensure Ajax are successful beyond just this season.

Youri Baas will likely play the majority of minutes for Ajax in the left centre-back position, and Blind will probably also get his fair share of minutes in that position, although he has not played since 13 August as he continues to recover from an injury.

Janse is also left-footed, and his minutes this season may therefore be limited, but Baas will likely leave in the next 12 months, whether that be in January or the summer. He already attracted interest from FC Porto and Eintracht Frankfurt last summer.

When Baas leaves, Ajax already have his successor in Janse. He has a lot of qualities to develop into a very good central defender, and Ajax extending his contract shows they have a long-term plan for him.

articles.title: Previewing the Boston Celtics preseason games for the 2026-27 campaign
articles.summary: There is plenty to learn about the incoming players joining the team, as well as the players on camp deals trying to earn a spot.
articles.body:
Previewing the Boston Celtics slate of preseason games for the 2026-27 campaign, it can be easy to be cynical given the contests do not count toward the regular season win total. But there is plenty to learn about the incoming players joining the team, as well as the players on camp deals trying to earn a spot on the regular or two roster.

And there will be no shortage of drama either, given Boston will square off with the Philadelphia 76ers , the team they traded star forward Jaylen Brown not once but twice in preseason action. Will Brown play at the home or away tilts, or will he save that smoke for when the contests count? And the Celtics will also face the new-look Cleveland Cavaliers and Charlotte Hornets as well. What can we learn about the team from these contests?

The hosts of the "First to the Floor" podcast, Jake Issenberg, Ben Vallis, and Wayne Spooney, took some time on a recent episode of their show to talk it over Check it out below!

articles.title: Yankees fans want 1 thing to immediately happen after ALDS loss to Rays
articles.summary: Fans of the New York Yankees are rioting again—on social media—after the team got swept by the Tampa Bay Rays in the ALDS on Wednesday. The Yankees lost to t...
articles.body:
Fans of the New York Yankees are rioting again—on social media—after the team got swept by the Tampa Bay Rays in the ALDS on Wednesday. The Yankees lost to the Rays, 4-3, in Game 3 at Yankee Stadium.

New York was eliminated in the ALDS for the second straight year.

The Yankees had their chances to extend the best-of-five series, but the Rays held on, highlighted by Victor Mesa Jr.'s go-ahead two-run home run in the top of the sixth inning.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

After the game, the biggest grievance of the fans of the Yankees was clear, as they trooped to X to air it out for all the world to see.

"Hear me out. Fire Aaron Boone . Hire CC Sabathia," said @Digital_Vix3n.

"Can the Yankees PLEASE fire Aaron Boone," echoed @stevenolguin212.

"Can we please move on from Aaron Boone after we get swept by the Rays? I don't ask about (Brian) Cashman anymore because Hal (Steinbrenner) is scared to fire him. Not sure what Cashman has on the family, but it's keeping him employed," wrote @bigpedro3636.

"Fire Aaron Boone. Either from his job or into the sun. Both work," posted @FannJames.

"Aaron Boone has been awful his entire tenure, but the mismanagement of that ALDS was by far his worst work," commented @josh3302.

Boone, who has been with the Yankees since 2018, signed a two-year, $15 million contract extension in 2025. He has been in the hot seat since last season due to New York's underwhelming finishes.

Before Game 3, ESPN's Stephen A. Smith predicted that Boone will be axed if they get booted out by the Rays.

The Yankees have advanced to the playoffs in eight of Boone's nine seasons.

articles.title: Home Team Friday Week 7 MVP
articles.summary: Lincoln City, Ind. (WEHT) – After counting up over 1,100 total votes, Heritage Hills’ Tyce Winchell was named our week seven Home Team Friday MVP of the nigh...
articles.body:
Lincoln City, Ind. (WEHT) – After counting up over 1,100 total votes, Heritage Hills' Tyce Winchell was named our week seven Home Team Friday MVP of the night.

The senior quarterback recorded 225 total yards of offense and five touchdowns in the Patriots 35-7 win over Mt. Vernon. He secured 78.8 percent of the votes to claim MVP.

"That's awesome. I mean yea, I've been in the running a lot but finally got it. It's great like all my hard work is paying off. I got great teammates and great coaches, I mean even if I'm making plays (I) can't do any of that without my teammates or my coaches. They help me out a lot."

Winchell and Heritage Hills will take on North Posey on Friday, October 9th.

articles.title: Aaron Boone sums up heartbreaking end to Yankees’ 2026 season
articles.summary: The New York Yankees are out of the 2026 postseason. Though New York’s season did not end without controversy, it has ended nonetheless. The Yankees were s...
articles.body:
The New York Yankees are out of the 2026 postseason. Though New York's season did not end without controversy , it has ended nonetheless. The Yankees were swept in the ALDS by the Tampa Bay Rays, who are off to the ALCS.

It was a whirlwind for New York this postseason. The Yankees dominated the Boston Red Sox in the AL Wild Card round. It didn't take much to brush aside their bitter rivals. The ALDS was a much different story, though. And the realization is setting in for manager Aaron Boone .

"The ending's terrible…it's a broken clubhouse…we just didn't hit enough to score enough and they did," Boone said, via Newsday Sports reporter Erik Boland.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The Yankees thought they had tied the game in the bottom of the sixth. Anthony Volpe swatted a ball that appeared to be a home run. However, it was later ruled an RBI double due to fan interference. This kept the Yankees down by a run.

The Rays would take this and run with it. Tampa was unable to build upon its lead, but it didn't need to. They held the Yankees scoreless for the remainder of the game and are off to the ALCS as a result.

New York certainly has a lot to assess this winter. Another unfortunate October failure is going to raise important questions in the Bronx. Boone's future in the dugout will certainly be a topic of discussion, as well. How the Yankees proceed this winter will be quite interesting to see.

articles.title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning
articles.summary: Top Fuel drag racing is the only elite motorsport class where women frequently beat men to major titles.
articles.body:
Like "being shot out of a cannon" is the closest comparison that driver Susanne Callin can come up with for the extreme motorsport she competes in.

She is a two-time European champion in Top Fuel drag racing - often described as the fastest sport on the planet.

Races begin with a bone-shaking roar, as the world's fastest-accelerating cars leave the starting line, flames bursting out of their exhaust pipes.

The cars surge to more than 300mph (483km/h) in races that last just four seconds, with drivers experiencing more g-force than an astronaut launching into space.

It is the only elite class of motorsport where women frequently beat men to major titles.

Women have won seven out of the past nine European Championships, while, until recently, female US driver Brittany Force held the world speed record in the sport. In comparison, it is 50 years since a woman even competed in a Formula 1 Grand Prix race.

Women account for about 10% of participants across motorsport, and just 4% of elite drivers, according to campaign group More Than Equal. However, they made up 20% of the drivers competing in this year's US and European Top Fuel seasons.

So why is this high-velocity motorsport bucking the trend?

More Than Equal has described drag racing as "the most gender-equal motorsport in the world". Top Fuel is its most extreme form, named in reference to the powerful nitromethane fuel the cars run on.

Races take place on a straight track, just 1,000 feet (305 metres) long. Usually, two cars race each other. The intense g-force hits in the first second of the race, as the cars go from stationary to 100mph, with a second gut punch following as the clutch fully engages about half-way through.

It can look terrifying. The adrenalin rush is "extremely addictive", Swedish driver Callin, aged 43, tells BBC Global Women. Concern over the risks "is always there" she says, but "the safety really does work". Drivers are highly protected and safety precautions have been boosted further after fatal crashes in nitromethane-fuelled cars in 2004 and 2008, with races reduced in length.

Even just watching from the stands is a visceral experience, with vibrations shaking your body and the ground. Spectators are advised to wear ear defenders - the noise is comparable in decibels to standing next to a fighter jet taking off.

The highest official speed ever reached in a Top Fuel drag race is over 346mph, compared to 231mph in a Formula 1 Grand Prix. Brakes alone cannot slow the cars fast enough, so parachutes are deployed from the car's rear at the finish. The abrupt halt is "like someone kicking you in the chest", says Callin. "You lose your breath."

Top Fuel drivers need lightning-fast reactions and the physical endurance to withstand the intense forces. Precision driving skills are crucial as constant tiny adjustments are needed to keep the car on track.

"It has to be instant reactions with everything," says Callin. "By the time you've thought about it, it's too late… You really have to be one with the car."

And drivers need sheer guts. As Callin's rival and friend, 32-year-old Swiss driver Jndia Erbacher, jokingly tells the BBC - it takes "balls".

Callin clinched her second successive European Top Fuel title in September at the Santa Pod drag strip near Northampton. It is the fourth year in a row that a female driver has won the title. Meanwhile in the US, the record-setting Brittany Force won the US championship - run by the National Hot Rod Association (NHRA) - in both 2017 and 2022.

Drag racing is "highly unusual" among motorsports, says Fran Longstaff, chief innovation officer at More Than Equal, which supports and campaigns for women in motorsports.

Seeing women competing and winning in the sport has become "normalised rather than treated as exceptional", she says, including with "sustained success" in Top Fuel.

Research she co-led into why drag racing leads the way for equality in motorsport did not identify physical or biological factors, she says.

Instead, she points to a "continuous stream of visible female role models", as well as the sport's "accessible grassroots structure, junior programmes, open pits and family-oriented, collaborative culture".

In drag racing, points out Callin, women started winning major races "decades and decades ago".

The best known is Shirley Muldowney, dubbed the "first lady" of drag racing. The first woman to gain a Top Fuel licence, Muldowney won the NHRA championship in 1977 and went on to become the first driver to win three titles, with further wins in 1980 and 1982.

She had to battle to be allowed to compete at high levels, and faced hostility at times from other competitors and fans, but is now lauded for her perseverance.

When the BBC spent time with Callin in the pits between races at Santa Pod, surrounded by roaring engines and the smell of burning rubber, she signed autographs for fans - young and old, male and female - as her team prepared her car.

"I never feel I've been underestimated or treated badly for being a woman - never," Callin says.

This is in stark contrast to the experiences of women seeking to enter Formula 1. Young female drivers have spoken about being deliberately pushed off karting tracks by male competitors, and facing sexist comments in person or online.

More Than Equal's research also highlights a close-knit, family-oriented, collaborative culture in drag racing.

Like many top drag racers, Callin is from a racing family. She has been involved since childhood, following in the footsteps of her father and uncle, who both raced competitively.

Similarly, Erbacher's father Urs was a three-time European Top Fuel champion. And Brittany Force is the daughter of John Force, who holds 16 NHRA drag racing titles.

Female drivers have also shown that success is possible in Top Fuel in the years after having children.

Callin took a break for more than a decade to raise her daughter and stepdaughters. It was when she returned, aged 35, that her career really began to flourish. Similarly, Finnish driver Anita Mäkelä has won the European championship four times – three of them after a six-year break focusing on her children and running her family's chicken farm.

For Callin, racing is ingrained in family life.

Her dad is still part of her team. Her husband, Keith Bartlett - sometimes referred to as the "godfather" of UK drag racing - runs Santa Pod Raceway. Two of their daughters were driving junior dragsters at 80mph before they were old enough to sit a standard driving test. The youngest, Jacqueline, is now 19 and racing in adult classes.

The culture is collaborative, despite fierce competition - evident at last year's championship, when Erbacher offered Callin spare parts after her car was damaged.

"We hate each other at the starting line, but we love each other at the finish line," Erbacher says.

Asked about safety, both Callin and Erbacher talk about having "respect" for the car and the risks.

Over the years, strict procedures and regulations in Top Fuel have evolved to improve safety.

Drivers wear fire-resistant suits and sit in highly protected cockpits. Even after dramatic accidents, drivers in many cases escape relatively unscathed. This includes Callin, who has had two major crashes, suffering a concussion and a bruised collar bone, but no lasting injuries.

She says serious accidents are a "very small percentage". Even so, she is still not sure she would be comfortable if her daughter wanted to race in Top Fuel, with its extreme speeds.

Erbacher says her father initially refused to let her race, but relented when she declared she would do it with or without his help. He now manages her team.

More Than Equal also points out that the financial barriers to participating in drag racing are lower than for some other motorsports.

It takes millions of pounds to reach Formula 1, requiring high levels of sponsorship. Elite drag racing is also expensive, but not on the same scale. At the lowest levels, accessible racing events called "track days" take place, where participants can turn up and drive their own ordinary cars.

In the biggest Top Fuel championships, drivers race for themselves and earn points based on how they perform against their competitors. The European championship consists of four events - two in the UK, and one each in Germany and Sweden - in which each driver takes part in six races. Prize funds are limited, mostly serving as a contribution towards costs.

The US championship is on a larger scale, with 20 events across the country. The NHRA has not published a breakdown of prize money, but according to drag racing website Competition Plus, there is $500,000 (£378,000) for the 2026 winner, and significant pots for winners of individual events throughout the season.

The US, Europe and Australia have all seen female drag racing champions, but in other parts of the world, the sport is less well established, Top Fuel is rare and the picture is more varied. Individual women are breaking barriers across a range of different motorsports, and in some countries female drivers are carving out space in drag racing.

Women have begun to make an impact in Brazil's popular drag racing scene, including Fabiola Dal Bo who has held a category record in recent years. A team in South Africa hosts all-female drag races, while the popular reality TV show The Fastest in Arabic has raised the profile of women racers in the Middle East.

In India, 35-year-old Uvashri Kannadasan Balajeyanthi has clinched victories over male rivals in India's major drag racing series, Valley Run, with wins across three different categories in events from 2022 to 2024.

Known as Octy Girl in reference to the modified Skoda Octavia she first raced in, she tells the BBC she has "mixed feelings" when her achievements are met with surprise: "Why do they have to get shocked? Anyone can drive, right?" But she adds "sometimes I feel proud… I'm breaking the barrier of being in a male-dominated sport".

Back in Europe, however, Callin says being a woman on the drag strip is "super-normal".

She describes winning the European championship two years running as a "massive achievement". And she is already looking towards her next goal: becoming the first person, male or female, to win the title three years in a row.

This is part of the Global Women series from the BBC World Service, sharing untold and important stories from around the globe

images.caption: Top Fuel drivers experience more g-force than an astronaut launching into space [Ben Feetham / Pitlane News]
Callin says she has never felt underestimated or treated badly for being a woman in drag racing [Remco Sheelings]
Top Fuel cars surge from zero to 100mph in less than a second [Callum Pudge]
Shirley Muldowney was the first woman to win the NHRA Top Fuel Championship [Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty Images]
Erbacher jokes that it takes "balls" to compete in Top Fuel [BBC]
Indian driver Uvashri Kannadasan Balajeyanthi first raced in a modified Skoda Octavia [BBC]

articles.title: Browns ‘Good News’ on Mason Graham Injury Revealed Before Week 5
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns got some good news when Mason Graham was seen at the team facility--without the usual tools of an injury. The post Browns ‘Good News’ on...
articles.body:
When last we saw Cleveland Browns star defensive lineman Mason Graham, he was hobbling his way to the locker room before halftime on Thursday night during the big win over the Steelers in Week 4. Anxiety in Northeast Ohio was high. Not only had Graham been the No. 5 pick in the 2025 NFL draft, but he had really begun playing like a guy worthy of that status, developing into a true game-wrecking stalwart of the Cleveland front. This was not the guy Browns faithful needed to see go down with a length knee problem.

After the game, members of the Browns media corps reported that Graham was on crutches and already in a knee brace. Indeed, the situation looked grim.

Browns Practices Will be Closely Watched

There was positivity by early Friday though, when reports emerged that Graham was not as badly injured as had been originally feared. MRIs showed there was nothing structurally wrong with Graham's knee and that surgery would not be necessary. Still, the presumption was that this would be a multi-week injury, and that Graham could be penciled out of the Week 5 game in New York against the Jets.

Except that, after a solid four days off following the win, the Browns did not sound like they're ready to rule out Graham altogether in Week 5. It's a longshot that he will play, but all coach Todd Monken would say on the situation is that Graham was not practicing on Wednesday. But he noted that Thursday was possible.

If Graham practices and feels good, there is nothing stopping the Browns from putting him back on the field. He certainly had a transformation after Wednesday's practice–he was seen in the locker room, without any accompanying medical equipment.

Cleveland.com reporter Ashley Bastock, speaking on 92.3 The Fan in Cleveland, had the details .

"It will be concerning if Mason Graham is out for any extended period of time. But, I will say, the good news today is that when we saw him after that Steelers game, he was on crutches, in a brace. Today, briefly saw him walk through the locker room—no crutches, no brace. So, that's a good sign.

"This could have been much worse. I'd be more worried if it was, him needing a procedure done and missing weeks and weeks and weeks. Like, that's not the situation. So, it could be worse, it is concerning any time you're missing the guy who was generating the most pressure on your defense. So, they're going to have to make up for it in other ways. But I feel like the defense has a good mentality about it. That's what you would hope for right now."

articles.title: Quentin Grimes receives praise from JJ Redick for his defensive focus
articles.summary: Lakers coach JJ Redick likes the defensive focus he's seen from Quentin Grimes lately.
articles.body:
While many people feel Quentin Grimes will be a nice addition to the Los Angeles Lakers ' roster and possibly earn a starting spot this season, some feel he won't make that much of an impact.

According to the doubters, Grimes is a solid offensive threat as a complementary player, but while he's a solid defender, he isn't that much better than average on the defensive end. There are also doubts about whether he can perform well in his presumptive role as a point-of-attack defender.

But Grimes has played fairly well in his first two preseason games of 2026. Coach JJ Redick gave him some praise , particularly for his defensive focus, after Tuesday's 124-98 loss to the Golden State Warriors.

"I think he's a guy that, if needed, can create some advantages and, for that second-side action, can finish advantages offensively," Redick told reporters. "I think his commitment to the defensive end has been really good throughout camp and in these first two games. We're excited about him."

On Monday, during L.A.'s 127-103 win over the Sacramento Kings, Grimes started and scored 16 points on 5-of-7 shooting from the field and 2-of-3 from 3-point range in 19 minutes. On Tuesday, he contributed 12 points on 3-of-8 overall shooting while adding three assists and one steal.

Last season, he averaged 13.4 points a game as a member of the Philadelphia 76ers. His 3-point shooting is a cause for mild concern -- he was at 33.4% from that distance after shooting 38.5% from downtown during the 2024-25 season -- but his ability to create off the dribble, not just for himself but also occasionally others, will be an asset.

The Lakers lack a legitimate third scoring threat after all the changes they made to their roster this summer. Grimes could step into that role if he improves his shooting efficiency and consistently makes good decisions with the basketball in his hands.

articles.title: Yankees Fans’ Actions After Anthony Volpe Home Run Call Go Viral During ALDS
articles.summary: The New York Yankees are playing for their playoff lives Wednesday night in the ALDS against the Tampa Bay Rays at Yankee Stadium in the Bronx.What could tur...
articles.body:
The New York Yankees are playing for their playoff lives Wednesday night in the ALDS against the Tampa Bay Rays at Yankee Stadium in the Bronx.

What could turn out to be the controversial play of their season occurred in the sixth inning when Anthony Volpe, who is starting his first game of the series, launched what many assumed was a game-tying two-run home run to left field with two outs.

However, the ball landed right before the top of the fence and a fan reached his hands just past the top of the wall to catch the ball and bring it in.

After a lengthy review, the umpires deemed it fan interference and ultimately took back the home run, allowed one run to score and placed Volpe on second base. The next batter, Spencer Jones, struck out, leaving the score at 4-3 instead of potentially 4-4.

Yankees Fans' Actions in Outfield Go Viral

While the play and call quickly surfaced on social media, what Yankees fans in the outfield decided to do in the moments after the call went viral as well.

Fans decided it would be a good idea to start throwing trash onto the field, which briefly delayed the game until someone could go out and pick up the trash around the warning track behind left fielder Victor Mesa Jr.

Via Foul Territory : "Fans are expressing their frustrations by throwing trash on the field."

"Not some Yankees fans throwing trash! WOW," a fan posted.

Another person said, "yearly tradition of Yankees fans clearly interfering with a ball and then throwing trash on the field when the play is correctly ruled."

Someone else added, "Yankees fans interfering with a ball clearly not going over the wall and then throwing trash on the field at the player you interfered with."

"And then they throw trash onto their own field?! Yup Yankee fans for you," one more fan commented.

articles.title: NFL Fantasy Football Week 5 2026 Start ‘Em Sit ‘Em: Running Back
articles.summary: Week 5 fantasy football lineups are becoming increasingly difficult to set as injuries, workload splits, and matchup changes create uncertainty across the ru...
articles.body:
Week 5 fantasy football lineups are becoming increasingly difficult to set as injuries, workload splits, and matchup changes create uncertainty across the running back position. Some of the league's most dependable backs remain obvious starts. However, several players carry enough risk to make fantasy managers think twice before locking them into their lineups. With every touch becoming increasingly valuable as the season progresses, making the right start-or-sit decisions could be the difference between another fantasy win and a frustrating Week 5 loss.

Jonathan Taylor has been one of the most reliable touchdown producers in fantasy football through the first four weeks. That makes him an easy player to keep in starting lineups. Taylor has already recorded three two-touchdown performances this season. Even more impressive, he accomplished the feat last week against a difficult Washington front. He rushed for 95 yards and two scores. The only concern has been his reduced involvement as a receiver. Taylor has totaled just six receiving yards over the past two games.

Still, Taylor remains locked into 20-plus carries and is an ever-present threat near the goal line. That volume gives him an extremely reliable fantasy floor while his touchdown upside provides a significant ceiling. He may not possess quite the same explosive fantasy ceiling as Jahmyr Gibbs or Bijan Robinson, but Taylor is arguably the next running back in line among the elite options.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The matchup also works in his favor. Pittsburgh has allowed the ninth-most fantasy points to running backs this season.

Chase Brown's rushing numbers from Week 4 were ugly. That said, fantasy football managers should pay close attention to what he did as a receiver. Brown managed only 10 rushing yards in Cincinnati's loss to Jacksonville. However, he exploded in the passing game, catching 11 passes for 71 yards.

That receiving workload could become even more important in Week 5. Ja'Marr Chase is dealing with a concussion. Tee Higgins is managing an adductor injury. If either or both are unavailable against Miami, Cincinnati could once again lean heavily on Brown as a safety valve and playmaker in the passing game.

Christian McCaffrey doesn't need a massive yardage total to remain an automatic fantasy football starter . McCaffrey rushed 15 times for 52 yards and a touchdown while catching three of five targets for 18 yards in San Francisco's 24-14 victory over Denver. Overall, McCaffrey finished with 18 touches and remains the clear lead back in San Francisco. That workload is the most important takeaway. Even when the efficiency isn't spectacular, McCaffrey's combination of rushing opportunities, receiving involvement, and goal-line work gives him one of the safest fantasy profiles in the league. He remains a must-start option heading into Week 5 against Seattle.

Jaylen Warren, PIT (vs. IND), James Cook III, BUF (@ LAR)

RJ Harvey enters Week 5 in a difficult situation because Denver's backfield remains firmly split. JK Dobbins and Harvey combined for just 65 rushing yards, with Dobbins continuing to handle more of the rushing work. Harvey did have a significant role in the passing game, leading Denver in both receptions and receiving yards. That gives Harvey some fantasy football appeal, particularly in PPR formats. Still, the uncertainty surrounding his rushing workload makes him difficult to trust.

Dobbins has the better opportunity for early-down work, while Harvey's value is tied more closely to passing-game involvement. Until the backfield distribution becomes clearer, fantasy managers should consider Harvey a risky start.

Alvin Kamara's status needs to be monitored closely after the veteran running back missed New Orleans' Wednesday practice. Kamara was a non-participant while dealing with a back issue. That creates immediate uncertainty ahead of Week 5. Missing a Wednesday practice doesn't automatically mean he will be unavailable Sunday. However, fantasy football managers cannot afford to ignore the development.

The risk is especially significant because Kamara's fantasy value depends heavily on his workload and receiving involvement. If his back issue limits his snaps or touches, his usual fantasy ceiling could disappear. Until there is more clarity, managers should approach Kamara cautiously and have a backup plan ready.

Will Shipley isn't an attractive fantasy football option based on his Week 4 workload alone. Shipley rushed six times for just 23 yards in Philadelphia's 24-20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams. Six touches weren't enough to generate meaningful production. His fantasy outlook could change if Saquon Barkley misses time with his hamstring injury. Still, that uncertainty is precisely why managers should be cautious. Unless Barkley is ruled out and Shipley's workload expands significantly, Shipley is better left on the bench in most formats.

Tony Pollard, TEN (vs. HOU), Woody Marks, HOU (@ TEN)

Week 5 is all about trusting volume and opportunity. Taylor, McCaffrey, and Brown have clear paths to production. Harvey, Kamara, and Shipley carry enough uncertainty to warrant caution. Monitor the final injury reports, but don't overthink the backs with secure workloads.
